# Glossary and notation {#sec-glossary}

| Term | Meaning in this handbook |
|---|---|
| Audit attribute | A characteristic retained for group comparisons; it need not be a model predictor |
| Baseline | The unchanged model or policy used as a comparator |
| Calibration | Agreement between stated probabilities and outcome frequencies in a defined population |
| Calibration data | A held-out data role used to fit a postprocessor or uncertainty procedure; not necessarily probability recalibration |
| Censoring | Incomplete observation of an event time; right censoring tells us the event time exceeds the last observed time |
| Clinical utility | The benefit and burden of using a prediction for a specified action |
| Conformal coverage | A probability statement about an uncertainty set containing a future outcome under a stated sampling contract |
| Counterfactual | An outcome or prediction under an intervention in a specified causal model |
| Coverage, automation | The proportion receiving an automated prediction rather than deferral |
| Coverage, interval | The proportion or probability of outcomes contained in prediction intervals |
| Demographic parity | Equal decision selection rates across declared groups |
| Discrimination | Ability to rank or distinguish outcomes; different from social discrimination |
| Distribution shift | A change between the distribution used to develop or evaluate a model and the distribution where it is used |
| Equal opportunity | Equal true-positive rates across groups for a defined positive outcome |
| Equalized odds | Equal conditional decision distributions across groups given the outcome; binary TPR and FPR parity |
| Estimand | The precise quantity an analysis is intended to estimate |
| Exchangeability | Invariance of a joint distribution under reordering; a key sampling condition for ordinary conformal arguments |
| External validation | Evaluation in data meaningfully separate from development, such as another setting or period, with the relationship described |
| Fairness through unawareness | Omitting sensitive inputs; this does not remove their proxies or establish fairness |
| Intersection | A subgroup defined by a combination of attributes |
| IPCW | Inverse-probability-of-censoring weighting, used under assumptions to account for incomplete observation |
| Landmark | A defined prediction time at which eligibility and available information are assessed |
| Leakage | Information entering fitting or evaluation in a way that is unavailable or inappropriate for the intended use |
| Multicalibration | Calibration across a specified, supported family of subpopulations and score regions |
| Net benefit | A decision-analytic comparison using stated relative values of true and false positive actions |
| Postprocessor | A fitted or fixed transformation of the output or use of a frozen base predictor |
| Prediction interval | A set intended to cover a future outcome; different from an interval for an estimated mean or parameter |
| Proxy outcome | A recorded quantity used to stand for another target, such as expenditure used to represent need |
| Retained risk | Error conditional on receiving an automated prediction under a selective policy |
| Selection rate | Proportion receiving the positive decision |
| Sensitive-input invariance | Lack of prediction change under a specified replacement of an input; not automatically a causal property |
| Support | Sufficient relevant data and positive observation probabilities to define or estimate a quantity |
| Validation, software | Checks that an implementation behaves according to its contract |
| Validation, clinical | Evidence about performance, applicability, and potentially effects in a specified clinical use; always state the actual study |

## Notation

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $X$ | Predictors available at the prediction time |
| $A$, $a$ | Audit attribute and a particular group value |
| $Y$ | Recorded outcome |
| $S=f(X)$ | Model score; in survival chapters, $S(t\mid X)$ instead denotes a survival function |
| $D$ | Decision or selected class |
| $Q$ | Automation retention indicator; $Q_i(v)$ in the survival chapter denotes a time quantile |
| $p_k$ | Source probability of class $k$ |
| $q_k$ | Adjusted class or policy probability, with its meaning declared |
| $t_a$ | Decision threshold for group $a$ |
| $T,C,U,\delta$ | Event time, censoring time, observed duration, and event indicator |
| $\tau$ | Evaluation horizon |
| $G$ | Censoring survival function in the IPCW formula; a subgroup set in the multicalibration discussion |
| $F_a,F_a^{-1}$ | Group prediction CDF and quantile function in regression transport |
| $\epsilon$ | A declared tolerance |
| $\eta$ | Target conformal miscoverage |
| $\alpha$ | Partial-transport parameter under the chapter's explicit convention |
| $\pi_a$ | Group prevalence in binary calibration; reference mass where explicitly defined for transport or averaging |
| $\lambda$ | A mixing weight, penalty, or optimisation multiplier, defined locally |

Some symbols have conventional meanings in more than one literature. The local definition governs each equation. In particular, automation coverage and interval coverage should never share an unlabeled column in a report.
